newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade at day's low.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade at day's low.

text.p: German shares ended thin bourse trade lower on Monday, taking a break after they reached record highs on Friday, with profit taking putting pressure on the market.
Dealers said the dollar's weakness against the mark had helped pull the market down and said weak volumes were partly due to the absence of some foreign players on holiday.
The dollar had fallen sharply under 1.51 marks on Friday and dollar weakness is seen as negative for German exporters.
Trade on Wall Street, watched closely for direction in the German market, is also expected to be subdued due to the Veterans' day holiday in the U.S., dealers said.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor dealings at a day's low of 2,728.32 points, down 11.51 points, or 0.42 percent.

Chemicals group BASF AG climbed in pre-bourse dealings after the company said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had given it conditional approval to market its Meridia TM obesity drug in the U.S..
But BASF lost ground in bourse dealings, to end down 34 pfennigs at 51.40 marks.
Drugs group Schering also lost ground, ending down 15 pfennigs at 124.10 marks, although the firm announced positive nine-month figures.
One of the day's biggest gainers was dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care, which touched a year high of 144.45 and ended bourse dealings up almost six percent, or 7.70 marks, at 143.80 marks.
Dealers said the stock was reacting belatedly to nine month results released on Friday. The company had also climbed in New York.
Shares in the world's largest reinsurance group, Munich Re, closed floor dealings down 65 marks, almost two percent, at 3,730 marks after the firm announced results for the 1995/96 financial year.

Meanwhile, state-owned telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG, part of which is due to be floated next week, said it had topped up the volume of its share issue to 600 million shares or three billion marks from 500 million shares or 2.5 billion marks.
Dealers said the news had pushed down the price of Telekom shares in "grey" or unofficial pre-flotation telephone dealings, to 33.00 to 33.50 marks, from 34 marks.
